analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the last-updated date, rewrites the GLM video description (head lines 810-813, 829) and adds GLM prompt-policy notes (head lines 876-880). The patch excerpt is truncated and mentions a range at head 1717-1726 that is not in the supplied units, so I could not examine it.

The video text changes the documented behavior. The provider now indexes variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks, timing frame i at i / nominalFrameRate, instead of refusing them with a 400. This widens the untrusted-media attack surface (A-001, TB-007), but the supplied evidence shows no source change. The docs still state the existing bounds: a 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes), the processor prepared-pixel cap of 28,532 visual tokens, VisionMemoryGate reservations, one video decoded at a time, and deterministic 400 refusals for processor errors. No regression is demonstrable from documentation alone. The follow-up question is whether the code enforces the decoded-frame cap before or during decode for variable-frame-rate tracks. A track with a pathological frame count or an inaccurate nominalFrameRate could inflate decode work. That code is outside this batch, so I recorded it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.

The new returned-reasoning and strict-tool notes describe validating each auto call against its schema before exposure. They also describe requiring the shipped template hash. These are neutral to positive.

The documented prefix-cache behavior is unchanged: media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture, and coordinator text prefix reuse is partitioned by cache scope. This leaves the T-041 posture unchanged. No new threat IDs or invalidated assumptions are apparent.
